product_advantages: Cable knit pattern adds texture and structure that holds shape through washes
Hand-finished seams eliminate bulk, suitable next-to-skin for newborns
Grade A 14.5–15.5μm Mongolian cashmere: 3x warmer per gram than merino wool
Custom monogram on beanie cuff edge (minimum 200 pcs per design)

faq.q: What ages does the cashmere baby set fit?
faq.a: The set fits newborns through approximately 24 months. The beanie measures 30–36 cm head circumference, and the booties fit foot length 8–11 cm. Custom sizes available for orders 500+ pcs.

faq.q: Is the cable knit pattern machine-made or hand-finished?
faq.a: The cable pattern is knitted on 12-gauge Shima Seiki flat knitting machines. Seams are then finished by hand on a stitch-by-stitch basis. This combination produces the cable definition that machine-only construction cannot match.

faq.q: What is the MOQ for private label baby cashmere sets?
faq.a: MOQ is 100 sets per design in standard colors. Custom Pantone colorways require 5kg+ per color and 200 sets minimum. Sample sets ship in 7 days at USD 60–120 per set, refundable against first bulk order.

faq.q: How should I wash the cashmere baby set?
faq.a: Hand wash cool (30°C max) with cashmere-specific shampoo. Reshape and lay flat to dry on a towel. Avoid wringing or tumble drying. The cable pattern retains its shape through 50+ gentle wash cycles when handled this way.

products.meta_description: Cashmere cable knit beanie for women in Grade A Mongolian cashmere. 12-gauge, fold-over cuff, hand-finished. Custom Pantone and logo embroidery available.
product_advantages: Cable needle transfers create 3D texture without bulk — flatter profile than typical aran beanies
Two-way fold-over cuff: full fold for ear coverage or pushed back for slouchy silhouette
60-80g per beanie: 3x warmer than merino wool per gram, no head heaviness
Hand-finished at cuff seam and pom attachment point — boutique construction quality
Custom Pantone colorways from 100 pcs, logo embroidery on cuff edge from 200 pcs

faq.q: What is the difference between this beanie and a typical aran beanie?
faq.a: Our cable is created through cable-needle transfers during machine knitting, producing a 3D twisted texture with less bulk than traditional aran cable patterns. A typical aran beanie weighs 100-120 g and has visible relief; this beanie weighs 60-80 g with a flatter, more elegant cable definition.

faq.q: Can I wear this beanie two ways?
faq.a: Yes. The fold-over cuff measures 7-8 cm, allowing two styles: fold the cuff fully down for ear coverage and warmth (the classic look), or push the cuff back for a slouchy beanie silhouette that sits further back on the head. Both styles preserve the cable definition.

faq.q: Is 60-80g per beanie heavier or lighter than typical wool beanies?
faq.a: Lighter than wool. A wool beanie of similar warmth typically weighs 100-150 g because wool fibers are denser. Cashmere's hollow fiber structure traps more air per gram, so less cashmere fiber is needed for the same insulation.

faq.q: How should I store this cashmere beanie during summer?
faq.a: Wash before storage (body oils attract moths). Fold (do not hang — hanging distorts shape). Store with cedar blocks or lavender sachets as natural moth repellent. Avoid plastic bags (trap moisture and cause yellowing). Inspect monthly for any moth activity in concealed areas like the cuff fold.

products.meta_description: Cashmere baby hat and sock gift set, Grade A Mongolian cashmere, plain knit, gift-packable. Custom Pantone and monogram from 200-300 sets.
product_advantages: Plain knit surface is gentler on newborn skin than cable or ribbed textures
Gift-packable in single kraft box with cotton tissue — ready for retail without extra packaging
2-ply 2/26 Nm yarn: 3x warmer than merino per gram, finished weight 45-55g beanie + 18-22g socks
Custom Pantone from 200 sets, custom monogram on beanie cuff from 300 sets
OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certified, no harmful substances on baby skin

faq.q: What ages is this gift set designed for?
faq.a: Newborns through 12 months. The beanie fits 32-36 cm head circumference, and the socks fit 8-10 cm foot length. Custom sizes for 12-24 month available on orders 500+ sets with extended lead time of 7-10 days.

faq.q: Can the gift box be customized with our brand logo?
faq.a: Yes. Logo-printed kraft boxes from 500 sets, custom-printed cotton tissue with logo from 1000 sets. Logo printing adds 7-10 days to lead time and USD 0.30-0.50 per set.

faq.q: What is the difference between this set and the cable knit baby set (hats-122)?
faq.a: This set uses plain knit, which produces a smoother surface suitable for newborn skin and gift presentation. The cable knit set (hats-122) includes booties and uses 3D cable texture, more textured but warmer for cooler climates. Both are OEKO-TEX certified. Choose plain knit for gift sets and newborn gifts, cable knit for colder-climate baby wear.

faq.q: Can the socks and beanie be sold separately?
faq.a: Yes. Plain knit beanie (hats-164-beanie) and plain knit baby socks (accessories-baby) are available as separate SKUs from 100 pcs per design. The gift set is the bundled SKU (hats-164) with kraft box packaging. Contact sales for separate SKU pricing.

faq.q: Why is this a 30/70 cashmere-merino blend rather than 100% cashmere?
faq.a: The 30/70 blend provides cashmere softness at the skin surface while delivering 25-35% cost savings vs 100% cashmere. Merino wool also provides more durability for everyday wear — important for B2B buyers targeting customers who want cashmere hand-feel but need a sweater that holds up to regular use. The blend is the most common cashmere entry point for B2B programs.

faq.q: What is the difference between 7-gauge and 12-gauge knits?
faq.a: 7-gauge knit is chunkier, more textured, with a heavier hand-feel — appropriate for FW collections, unisex lines, and textured cable patterns. 12-gauge knit is finer, smoother, more refined — appropriate for dressier pullovers and women basic collections. The same cable pattern looks more dimensional at 7-gauge than 12-gauge.

faq.q: What is the MOQ for custom Pantone colors?
faq.a: Custom Pantone colors from 100 pcs per design. Lab dip in 5-7 days, bulk production 30-40 days for custom orders. Custom intarsia graphics, embroidered logos, and custom trims from 200 pcs. Mixed sizes within a single style allowed at no surcharge.

faq.q: Is this sweater machine-washable?
faq.a: We recommend hand wash cool (30°C max) with cashmere-wool detergent for longest life. Machine washing on a delicate/wool cycle at 30°C is acceptable if the sweater is in a mesh laundry bag and the spin cycle is disabled. Lay flat to dry on a towel. Do not tumble dry. With proper care, the sweater will last 5+ years of regular wear.

faq.q: What is the difference between a turtleneck and a crew neck?
faq.a: A turtleneck has a high folded collar that covers the neck — typically 18-22 cm in folded height. A crew neck sits at the base of the neck with no fold. Turtlenecks sell at a 10-15% premium due to the additional knitting and finishing of the collar. Turtlenecks are most popular for FW collections and as office/business casual layering.

faq.q: Will the turtleneck collar lose its shape over time?
faq.a: Our double-thickness collar construction is designed to retain shape over years of wear. The folded edge is a separate knitted component attached during linking, with the same yarn count as the body. With proper care (hand wash, lay flat dry, fold for storage), the collar will maintain its fold and shape for the life of the sweater.

faq.q: Custom collar height is possible?
faq.a: Yes. Standard folded height is 18-22 cm. Custom collar heights from 15-25 cm available from 200 pcs per design. Some B2B buyers prefer lower-height turtlenecks (15-18 cm) for unisex collections, and higher (22-25 cm) for dramatic FW pieces. Custom collar heights require 7-10 days extra sampling time.

faq.q: Is this sweater suitable for sensitive skin?
faq.a: Yes. 100% cashmere at 14.5–15.5μm is well below the 20μm threshold that typically causes skin irritation. The 12-gauge knit gives a smooth surface against the skin. We have 14 years of supply to European luxury brands with no reports of skin sensitivity. For customers with diagnosed wool allergies, sampling is recommended (some people react to lanolin traces in any wool-based yarn, including cashmere).

products.meta_description: Long-line wool cashmere turtleneck pullover, 7-gauge knit, 30% cashmere / 70% merino, 420-500g. Tunic length. Custom Pantone from 100 pcs.
product_advantages: Long-line tunic length (75-85 cm): provides coverage for leggings and tight pants
30/70 cashmere-merino blend: cashmere softness, merino durability, 25-35% cost savings vs 100% cashmere
7-gauge chunky knit: substantial feel without heavy weight for FW collections
Turtleneck collar 18-22 cm folded: double-thickness for shape retention
Hand-linked seams at shoulders and armholes for retail-quality presentation

faq.q: What length is the long-line version?
faq.a: The long-line pullover measures 75-85 cm at size M (varies by size). Standard pullovers are typically 64-68 cm. The long-line version sits at mid-thigh, providing extra coverage. The 7-10 cm additional length compared to standard pullover makes it suitable for wearing with leggings, leggings-pants, or as a tunic-style layer over dresses.

faq.q: Why is this a 30/70 blend rather than 100% cashmere?
faq.a: The 30/70 blend provides cashmere softness at the skin while delivering 25-35% cost savings vs 100% cashmere. Merino wool also provides more durability for everyday wear. The blend is the most common cashmere entry point for B2B buyers. The 7-gauge knit also benefits from merino's elastic recovery, which helps the long-line silhouette hold shape.

faq.q: What is the MOQ for custom colors?
faq.a: Custom Pantone colors from 100 pcs per design. Custom long-line length from 100 pcs. Custom collar height from 200 pcs. Lab dip in 5-7 days, bulk production 30-40 days for fully custom orders. Mixed sizes within a single style allowed at no surcharge.

faq.q: Is this suitable for cold weather wear?
faq.a: Yes. The 7-gauge knit with 30/70 cashmere-merino blend provides substantial warmth for FW wear (autumn and winter). The long-line silhouette provides extra core coverage. For below -10°C conditions, layer with a base layer. For most B2B markets (EU/US/JP), this is the appropriate FW weight category.

faq.q: What is the difference between this pashmina and a regular scarf?
faq.a: A pashmina is wider and longer than a standard scarf, designed for shoulder draping. This shawl measures 200x70 cm vs a typical scarf at 180x35 cm or 190x45 cm. The extra width allows it to be worn over the shoulders as a light layer without folding, or wrapped twice at the neck for a fuller silhouette.

faq.q: Is cashmere pashmina warmer than wool pashmina?
faq.a: Cashmere pashmina is warmer per gram than wool pashmina, but the fabrics are typically lighter overall. A wool pashmina of equivalent size weighs 280-350 g; this cashmere pashmina weighs 180-220 g. Since cashmere traps 3x more air per gram, the lighter cashmere version provides equivalent or better insulation at less weight.

faq.q: Can I order custom sizes or prints?
faq.a: Custom sizes from 180x60 cm to 220x90 cm available from 100 pcs per design. Custom digital print (Pantone-matched) available from 200 pcs per design. Custom Pantone solid colors from 5kg+ per color. Lab dip in 5-7 days, bulk production 20-30 days after approval.

faq.q: How should I wash this cashmere shawl?
faq.a: Hand wash cool (30°C max) with cashmere-specific shampoo. Reshape and lay flat to dry on a towel. Avoid wringing or tumble drying. Dry clean is safe for tough stains. The fabric retains drape and softness through 50+ gentle wash cycles when handled this way.

faq.q: What is the difference between this blanket scarf and a standard scarf?

faq.q: Why is this knit instead of woven?
faq.a: Knitting gives a more textured, dimensional surface than weaving, with better stretch and recovery. The cable + plain knit panel combination creates visual interest on both sides of the shawl. The 7-gauge knit also produces a warmer hand-feel due to the higher yarn volume per square inch.

faq.q: Will the knit stretch out with wear?
faq.a: Cashmere knit has natural recovery — it stretches under wear and returns to shape after washing. Woolen-spun yarn is more forgiving than worsted-spun. To maintain shape, fold (do not hang) for storage, and dry flat after washing. With proper care, the shawl will hold its shape for years.

products.meta_description: Plain woven cashmere shawl wrap, 200x100 cm, Grade A Mongolian cashmere, 2/48 Nm worsted, 200-260g. Custom digital print from 200 pcs.
product_advantages: Plain 1/1 weave: smooth, even surface — most refined dressy interpretation
200x100 cm wide-format: full shoulder coverage for evening wear and resort
Finished weight 200-260 g per shawl: substantial without heavy
Fulling process gives characteristic softness and drape after weaving
Custom digital print available from 200 pcs (allowed by plain weave surface)

faq.q: What is the difference between this and a pashmina scarf?
faq.a: A pashmina scarf is typically 200x70 cm. This shawl wrap is 200x100 cm — wider for full shoulder coverage. The plain weave also gives a smoother, more dressy appearance than the textured pashmina-style formats. Wear this for evening events; wear the pashmina for casual layering.

faq.q: Why is the plain weave more expensive than textured weaves?
faq.a: Plain weave requires finer yarn tension control and tighter quality inspection — any yarn inconsistency shows immediately on the smooth surface. The yarns themselves are also typically finer (2/48 Nm or 2/60 Nm) for a more refined drape. The combination of finer yarn and tighter inspection adds 10-15% to the per-unit cost.

faq.q: Can I order custom prints on this shawl?
faq.a: Yes. The plain weave surface is ideal for digital print — printed designs read clearly without texture interference. Custom digital print from 200 pcs per design. Up to 8 Pantone colors per design included; 9-12 colors adds USD 0.20-0.40 per piece. Lab dip in 5-7 days, bulk production 30-40 days.

faq.q: How do I remove wrinkles from this shawl after shipping?
faq.a: Steam is the safest method. Hang the shawl in a steamy bathroom for 10-15 minutes, or use a handheld steamer held 10+ cm from the fabric. Avoid direct ironing. For deep wrinkles, low-temperature iron (110°C max) with a pressing cloth between iron and cashmere. The shawl will smooth naturally after hanging for a few hours.

faq.q: What is the difference between winter and regular cashmere socks?
faq.a: Winter-weight cashmere socks use a higher yarn count (2/26 Nm woolen-spun) for more loft and warmth. Regular-weight socks use finer yarn (2/48 Nm worsted-spun) for thinner, dressier socks. The winter version is suitable for boots and cold-weather wear; the regular version is suitable for dress shoes and office wear.

faq.q: Will the seamless knit lose shape over time?
faq.a: Seamless knit on Italian Lonati machines produces a more durable fit than cut-and-sew knit because there are no seams to unravel. The woolen-spun yarn maintains shape through 50+ wear cycles when hand-washed and laid flat to dry. For maximum life, wash in a mesh laundry bag with cashmere shampoo.

faq.q: What is the MOQ for custom colors?
faq.a: Custom Pantone colors from 100 pcs per design (mixed leggings and socks combined). Custom sizes from 100 pcs per size run. Custom waistband height from 200 pcs. Lab dip in 5-7 days, bulk production 30-40 days for fully custom orders. Mixed sizes within a single style allowed at no surcharge.

faq.q: Are these suitable for travel?
faq.a: Yes. Cashmere's natural temperature regulation and anti-odor properties make it ideal for travel — it can be worn multiple times between washes, packs small, and provides warmth without bulk. The seamless knit prevents rubbing during long flights or drives. Many B2B buyers in the EU and US see strong demand for travel sets.

faq.q: What is the difference between high rib and regular knit stockings?
faq.a: High rib knit has a 2x1 rib structure at the cuff (alternating knit and purl stitches) that creates vertical stretch. The rib structure holds the stockings up without needing elastic bands. Regular knit stockings (without rib) require elastic at the top to stay up. Rib knit also provides a more refined, classic dress-sock appearance.

faq.q: Will the ribs lose stretch over time?
faq.a: The 2x1 rib structure has natural recovery — it stretches under wear and returns to shape after washing. Cashmere's natural elasticity helps the rib hold its shape. Wash in a mesh laundry bag with cashmere shampoo and lay flat to dry. Do not tumble dry or hang dry (which can stretch the rib permanently).

faq.q: What is the MOQ for custom colors?
faq.a: Custom Pantone colors from 100 pcs per design. Custom sizes from 50 pcs per size run. Custom cuff height from 200 pcs. Lab dip in 5-7 days, bulk production 30-40 days for fully custom orders.

faq.q: Are these suitable for sensitive skin?
faq.a: Yes. 100% cashmere at 14.5–15.5μm is well below the 20μm threshold that typically causes skin irritation. The seamless tubular knit construction means no seam contact against the skin. OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certified. Suitable for customers with sensitive skin or wool allergies in most cases.

product_advantages: 12-gauge circular knit: smooth, refined surface suitable for innerwear and outerwear
Reinforced elastic waistband: shape retention through repeated wear and washing
Ankle-shape leg openings: refined silhouette, suitable for layering under tunics
Single-piece orders available: just leggings or just pants as separate SKUs
OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certified: no harmful substances, suitable against skin

faq.q: What sizes are available in this set?
faq.a: EU sizes 32-46 standard, equivalent to US 0-14 / UK 4-18. Custom sizes available from 100 pcs per design. Single-piece orders also available as separate SKUs (just leggings or just pants) for stores that want to mix and match within a collection.

faq.q: Is this suitable for loungewear or outerwear?
faq.a: Both. The plain knit construction gives a refined surface suitable for innerwear layering (under tunics or long sweaters) and loungewear. The 200-280 g weight is appropriate for travel and home wear. For outerwear, layer with a long tunic or sweater — the cashmere surface is refined enough to wear without being hidden.

faq.q: Will the elastic waistband lose stretch over time?
faq.a: Our reinforced elastic waistband is designed for 2+ years of regular wear. Maintain shape by washing in a mesh laundry bag and laying flat to dry (do not tumble dry). Hand wash cold for longest life. The waistband is replaceable — we can ship replacement elastic for orders of 50+ pieces.

faq.q: What is the MOQ for custom colors?
faq.a: Custom Pantone colors from 100 pcs per design. Custom sizes from 100 pcs. Custom waistband height (lower, mid, high rise) from 200 pcs. Lab dip in 7-10 days, bulk production 30-40 days for fully custom orders.

faq.q: What is the difference between woolen-spun and worsted-spun yarn?
faq.a: Woolen-spun yarn is carded and air-jet or mule spun, giving a random fiber alignment, loftier appearance, and softer hand-feel. Worsted-spun yarn is combed and ring-spun, giving parallel fiber alignment, smoother surface, and more refined drape. Woolen-spun is more forgiving for hand-knitting (less splitting, more forgiving gauge); worsted-spun is better for structured garments.

faq.q: How many socks can I knit from 100g of yarn?
faq.a: A 100g skein of 2/26 Nm yarn knits approximately one pair of adult socks (size 38-42) at 7-9 gauge. For a longer pair (knee-high), plan 150-200g per pair. For baby socks, 50g makes 2-3 pairs. The exact yardage depends on stitch gauge and pattern; we recommend ordering 10% extra to account for swatching and any rework.

faq.q: Can I order undyed yarn for hand-dyeing?
faq.a: Yes. We ship undyed (greige) yarn in 1kg cones for hand dyers and small studios. Pricing is 15-20% below dyed stock colors. Minimum order 5 kg per count. Lead time 7-10 days for stock counts. Custom greige counts from 50 kg with 30-40 day lead time.

faq.q: What is the best needle size for hand knitting this yarn?
faq.a: For 2/26 Nm woolen-spun cashmere at 7-9 gauge (typical for socks and scarves), use 3.5-4.5 mm needles (US 4-6). For tighter gauge (10-12 gg for finer fabrics), use 2.5-3.25 mm (US 1-3). The woolen-spun yarn is more forgiving than worsted-spun, so gauge variation is acceptable up to 1/2 stitch per inch.

faq.q: What does superwash mean?
faq.a: Superwash is a chemical treatment that removes the outer scales of wool fiber, preventing felting. Treated yarn can be machine-washed without felting or shrinking. Chlorine-free processes (H2O2 or enzymatic) are preferred for environmental reasons. The treatment does not affect the natural hand-feel of the wool; it only removes the felting tendency.

faq.q: Is superwash safe for sensitive skin?
faq.a: Yes. Our chlorine-free superwash process is OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certified, meaning no harmful substances remain in the yarn. The cashmere component (30%) provides additional softness for sensitive skin. Some customers with very severe wool allergies may still react to any wool-based yarn, regardless of superwash treatment, due to residual lanolin traces.

faq.q: What is the MOQ for custom colors?
faq.a: Custom Pantone colors from 5 kg per color. Custom count from 2/36 to 2/60 Nm available from 50 kg. Lab dip in 5-7 days, bulk production 30-40 days for custom orders. Mixed dye lots within a single color accepted at no surcharge.

faq.q: Can I machine-wash garments made from this yarn?
faq.a: Yes. Garments made from this superwash yarn can be machine-washed on a delicate/wool cycle at 30°C with cashmere-wool detergent. Lay flat to dry. Do not tumble dry. The superwash treatment prevents felting, but air-drying is still recommended for longest life. The garment will soften with washes over time.

faq.q: What is the difference between 50/50 and 30/70 cashmere-merino blends?
faq.a: The 50/50 blend has higher cashmere content (50% vs 30%), giving softer hand-feel and more warmth per gram. The 30/70 blend is more durable and less expensive. The 50/50 ratio is the sweet spot for B2B buyers who want more cashmere hand-feel without the price of 100% cashmere. The 50/50 is approximately 20-30% more expensive than 30/70.

faq.q: What is the best needle size for hand knitting this yarn?
faq.a: For 2/48 Nm worsted-spun yarn at 10-12 gauge (typical for sweaters and scarves), use 3.25-4 mm needles (US 3-6). For 14-gauge knits (finer fabrics, lace), use 2.5-3 mm (US 1-3). The 50/50 blend is more forgiving than 100% cashmere, so gauge variation is acceptable up to 1/2 stitch per inch.

faq.q: Is this yarn suitable for baby garments?
faq.a: Yes. The 50/50 blend is appropriate for baby garments — cashmere provides softness for sensitive skin, merino provides durability for washing. The OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certification confirms no harmful substances. Hand-washing is recommended for baby garments (machine washing on delicate cycle is acceptable but air-drying is gentler).
